subject.title: Feature Request: tools.cron.tools.deny config option for cron job tool restrictions

question: Should OpenClaw add a cron-scoped tool policy such as `tools.cron.tools.allow/deny`, make cron inherit `tools.subagents.tools`, or keep cron restricted only by per-job `payload.toolsAllow` and delivery-mode safeguards?
rationale: This choice defines a public config and authorization boundary for scheduled automation, including whether existing cron jobs keep today’s message-tool behavior or become subject to a new inherited/global deny layer.

options.title: Add explicit cron policy
options.body: Add a typed cron policy layer with deny-wins precedence against existing tool policy layers and per-job `toolsAllow`, plus docs and regression tests.

options.title: Rely on per-job allowlists
options.body: Keep the existing `payload.toolsAllow` / `openclaw cron --tools` path as the supported hard restriction and document that cron does not inherit subagent policy.

options.title: Inherit subagent policy
options.body: Treat cron like delegated execution by applying `tools.subagents.tools`, accepting the compatibility risk for existing scheduled jobs.

recommendation.title: Add explicit cron policy
recommendation.body: Add a typed cron policy layer with deny-wins precedence against existing tool policy layers and per-job `toolsAllow`, plus docs and regression tests.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete authored the prior detailed issue review and is the clearest routing owner for the unresolved config/security-boundary decision in this thread.
